marketSignals.title: Inference economics is becoming the next battleground
marketSignals.summary: The market is shifting from training-only scarcity toward production inference economics, where latency, utilization, geography, and cost per outcome matter.

marketSignals.title: Neoclouds are becoming full infrastructure platforms
marketSignals.summary: AI-native clouds are moving beyond GPU rental into purpose-built data centers, orchestration, networking, and developer-facing inference services.

marketSignals.title: Power and grid access constrain expansion
marketSignals.summary: Power availability, grid interconnection, and high-density cooling are material constraints for new AI infrastructure.

marketSignals.title: Capital intensity creates capacity moats
marketSignals.summary: The scale of compute, power, and data-center investment makes access to financing and long-term capacity a structural entry barrier.

marketSignals.title: Open and sovereign AI remains a strategic counterweight
marketSignals.summary: Open-weight models and regional infrastructure are being positioned as alternatives to dependence on a small set of closed frontier providers.

marketSignals.title: Partner concentration is a material ecosystem risk
marketSignals.summary: Heavy dependence on a small group of chip, cloud, power, and model partners can create concentration and negotiation risk; specific claims require ongoing verification.
